title: Cain didn’t just kill Abel—he ignored multiple warnings first (Genesis 4:6–7)
paragraphs: Cain didn’t just kill Abel—he ignored multiple warnings first (Genesis 4:6–7)
Cain didn’t just murder his brother.
He rehearsed it in his heart first.

God warned him before the blood hit the ground:
“Why are you angry? … Sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is for you, but you must rule over it.” (Genesis 4:6–7)

Cain was not blindsided.
He was confronted.
Checked.
Warned.
Invited to master what was trying to master him.

And that is how sin works.
It rarely starts with the scandal everyone sees.
It starts with the mood you keep feeding.
The jealousy you won’t name.
The offense you keep polishing.
The bitterness you let sit at the table.

Abel died in the field.
But Cain’s fall began long before that.

Here’s what we miss:
God’s warning was mercy.

Before judgment, there was counsel.
Before exposure, there was a chance to repent.
Before the act, there was a door still open.

That means this text is not only about Cain.
It is about us.

Every time God convicts you, that is mercy.
Every time Scripture cuts deep, that is mercy.
Every time the Spirit says, “Stop. Don’t go there,” that is mercy.
Ignore that voice long enough, and the sin at the door will become the sin in the house.

Jesus stepped into the story sinners like Cain wrote.
Not to excuse sin.
To crush its power.
To call murderers, addicts, liars, hypocrites, and religious performers to repentance and new life.
His blood speaks a better word than Abel’s blood ever could—not crying for vengeance, but offering forgiveness to all who repent and believe.

So do not play with the warning.
Do not baptize your anger.
Do not pet the thing God told you to kill.
Run to Christ while the door of mercy is still open.
